newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Cut aimed at underpinning market rate drop - SNB.
newsitem.headline: Cut aimed at underpinning market rate drop - SNB.

text.p: The Swiss National Bank (SNB) decided to cut its discount rate as a means of underscoring the recent decline in money market rates, an SNB spokesman said.
"The (rate cut) move is more a reassurance to the market that the interest rate decline since August will not be reversed," Swiss National Bank spokesman Werner Abegg said.

The central bank said today it was cutting its discount rate by 50 basis points to 1.0 percent. The discount rate was last cut to this low level in February 1978. It was subsequently raised to 2.0 percent in November 1979.

The SNB pointed out in its statement that it had been supplying the money market with additional liquidity since the beginning of August "in order to prevent monetary strain" and as a result, some money market rates fell below the discount rate.
"By lowering the discount rate, the Swiss National Bank underlines its expectation that the interest rate decline will continue for some time," it added. -- Zurich Editorial +41 1 631 7340
